pr_title: Selection Code Cleanup and Double Click Delimiter Runs
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

Just some housekeeping work on our selection. Added a few more tests and refactored some of the functionality to improve code clarity. 

Reenabled x86 tests. They work on my machine. I hope they work on CI?

Added support for double clicking delimiter runs.

Double Click Delimiter runs now operate as follows. Characters are separated into 3 classes:
- class 0: spaces and control characters
- class 1: delimiters imported from settings
- class 2: all other characters
If you double click a cell, the selection will expand until the class of the next cell differs from the preceding one.

This is slightly different than before in that the following example will only highlight the ">" char instead of the ">" and all the surrounding spaces:
```
C:\Terminal>
           ^
double click here
```

## References
N/A


## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #1327 
* [x] Closes #2261 
* [x] Closes #2206 
* [x] CLA signed
* [x] Tests added/passed
* [x] ~Requires documentation to be updated~
* [x] I am a core contributor

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments
Added some testing to ensure we don't crash on out-of-bounds selection anchors.
Consolidated the vertical offset for the anchors since they're always the same.
Broke up `GetSelectionRects()` into a more clear format with several helper methods.

## Validation Steps Performed
All tests pass. I manually did some ALT+selections and regular selections w/ and w/out the scroll area and it still seems fine.

NOTE: Double Click Delimiter runs in this isn't quite right yet. Dustin and I agreed on a new model:
handle delimiter runs as different delimiter classes where...
- ' ' --> class 0
- delimiters --> class 1
- otherwise --> class 2

double clicking a cell containing class `I` expands the selection to (exclusive) the first non-`I` class cell in both directions.

~This will be implemented in a new branch that targets this one, BUT will (probably) go into master as two different commits.~ This was easy. New commit covers this. Updating all other things about this PR.

review_comments: else THROW_HR(E_NOTIMPL)?
one still needs to expand for wide glyphs though

There's also a third `SelectionExpansionMode` (`Cell`). But in that case, we specifically don't expand. I'm not really a fan of `if(_multiClickSelectionMode == SelectionExpansionMode::Cell) { /* do nothing */ }` though.

@carlos-zamora @DHowett-MSFT side note: The check for cell here with a do nothing is kind of ugly but it does tell future devs looking at the code that the "cell" case was considered.   One thing I miss in the MSVC C++ compiler is the [-Wswitch-enum](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/DiagnosticsReference.html#wswitch-enum) warning in clang.  If the compiler had this warning then you could make this a switch statement and cover each enum case. (including the Cell's do nothing case) When this flag is used it really helps by giving you compile errors when enum values are added.   It forces you to look at each usage and fix potential errors.

Since the compiler doesn't yet support this we don't have that luxury.   Even so I think adding the do nothing case is still useful for future developers who don't know the history of the code.

I did a quick check and MSVC does support this warning - [C4062](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/error-messages/compiler-warnings/compiler-warning-level-4-c4062?view=vs-2019), but it is off by default.   It is a shame because this warning can be very useful when adding new values to enums/enum classes.
Should this be `position` or `positionWithOffsets`?
`positionWithOffsets`. I want it to return the clamped value. Safer overall.
Probably a few log subcomments here too so we can see which specific subcase failed.
